params.body:
## What was wrong

A trend reaches its signals through the concepts behind its patterns: up to eight signals per concept for fifteen concepts, plus three per related concept. The writer sees the best fifteen and writes the headline from those. Everything else is a candidate.

gentells.com listed and counted every candidate. Take "Young Adult Gamers Flag Studios That Hide AI in Their Games" (insight-2026-11-12-edd8d4fe). It went up with 85 signals from 50 sources in 6 regions, and "seen 1,440 times since March". The support judge had already rated its signals: 6 support it, 20 support part of it, 59 are unrelated. The unrelated ones include a Beijing taxi driver, airport biometrics and AI homework on Bilibili.

The 91 trends on the radar list 4,108 signals between them. 566 of those support their trend outright, 810 in part, and about two-thirds are unrelated.

The Gentells Standard already says only supporting signals count, "here and in every number below" (rules/trend.json#support). The verdicts were there, but the site never used them.

## What changes

- **`trendEvidence`** (support-store.mjs): a trend's evidence is the signals it holds that a judge found to support it, outright or in part, with the outright ones first.
- **`siteTrendRows`**: a trend is on the site when its evidence holds (rules/trend.json#holds), was seen at least 5 times on platforms, and was seen in the last 30 days. A trend nobody judged waits for its verdicts.
  - The candidate counts are still a cheap first filter, so verdicts are read only for the trends that might pass.
- **The card and the reading** (`listShowcaseInsights`, `getInsightReading`): signal, source and platform counts, kinds and spark are counted over the evidence.
- **The signal list** (`trendSignalsForSite` with `evidence`): only the evidence, outright first, and each signal carries its `verdict`. The regions and the graph follow, since both are built from that list.
- **The record** (`recurrenceFor` with `outright`): it counts only the concepts that at least two outright-supporting signals mention, not every concept the patterns hold.

### Inflow does not set the mix

A third of the radar named China. 24 of the 91 trends are about China only, and 7 more mix China in.

The cause is volume. The Chinese hot-search lists are read every half hour, fifty entries at a time, and `worker-china.mjs` enriches them ahead of the queue. On top of that, the site sorts by the last day a trend was seen, and those lists are always the freshest.

- **`LANES` and `laneOf`** (trend-origin.mjs): a trend is in the `east-asia` lane when at least half its evidence comes from East Asia, counted by the adapter's country or the source's region, never the classifier's tags.
- **The projection** gives each trend its `lane`, and gives the payload the `lanes` with the label and line the site shows over the band.
- **`laneRoom`** (insight-economy.mjs): a lane may take at most a quarter of a day's births (`TW_LANE_BIRTH_SHARE`, default 0.25). Suggest asks before writing (`worthWriting`), so a refusal costs no model call, and again before minting.

## Rollout

Nothing in the store changes. The verdicts exist, and this only reads them, so reverting the merge gives the old numbers back.

All 91 trends on the radar are judged already. Under the new rule, 38 stay, 11 of them in the East Asia lane. 53 leave:
- 17 are leads, without enough support;
- 27 have fewer than 5 platform sightings among their supporting signals;
- 9 have no recent ones.

That is more than half, so the site's delete brake (`gentells.max_delete_share`, 0.5) will refuse the first trends reconcile after this merge, and the site keeps its current cards. Lift it once on the site box after merging:

```
php artisan tinker --execute="config(['gentells.max_delete_share' => 0.7]); echo app(App\Services\Projection::class)->reconcileTrends();"
```

After that, the five-minute reconcile runs under the normal brake again. A trend that leaves comes back by itself once its evidence holds and is seen again.

## Tests

- New: `test/trend-evidence.test.mjs` (6 tests):
  - only evidence is listed and counted, outright first;
  - a trend that is unjudged, a lead, or seen too seldom stays off;
  - the record counts what the evidence shares;
  - the East Asia lane and its labels;
  - the lane's quarter of a day's births.
- Existing tests that build site trends without verdicts now mark their signals with `evidenceMarker` (test/helpers.mjs), so each stays about its own subject.
- Full suite 1672/1672, tsc clean.

Merge before the site PR, which reads `lane` and `lanes`. The site on its own changes nothing: without a lane, every trend stays in the main list.
params.title: Trends on gentells.com rest on the signals that bear them out; East Asia gets its own lane
